title: Rama's word
hook: a feud built on a sealed cave, and a promise that has to prove itself
carry: a promise given once is kept

segments.voice: Yesterday: Sita's jewels came out, Lakshmana knew only the anklets, and we saw why touching an elder's feet is honor.

Rama has promised to kill Vali. Sugriva has a question he's too polite to ask out loud: can you? Vali is famous. He's so strong he used to stride between the eastern and western seas before sunrise. Sugriva has watched that strength up close, and he has run from it. A friend with a bow is good news, but he needs to know this friend is enough. So Sugriva tells a story. And then he points at some trees.
screen: `A QUESTION TOO POLITE TO ASK.` → `A STORY, THEN SOME TREES.`

segments.voice: First, the story of the brothers. Vali, the elder, ruled Kishkindha, and Sugriva served him. One night a demon named Mayavi came to the gate shouting a challenge. Vali chased him into a huge cave and told Sugriva to wait at the mouth. A long time passed. Then blood came foaming out, and Sugriva heard the demon roar but not his brother. Sure Vali was dead, he sealed the cave with a boulder and went home, and the ministers made him king. But Vali had won. He came out, found the cave blocked and his brother on his throne, believed he'd been betrayed, and drove Sugriva out. Then the test. Sugriva shows Rama the dried skeleton of a buffalo demon Vali once killed, and Rama flicks it far away with his toe. It's dry now, Sugriva says politely. So he points to seven huge sala trees. Rama fires once. The arrow goes through all seven, through the hill behind them, into the earth, and back to his quiver. Sugriva falls at his feet. Notice what he was really asking. He never doubted Rama's heart; he needed to know the promise could be kept. And keeping a promise is what the tradition loves most about Rama. Back in Ayodhya, Valmiki has Rama tell Kaikeyi: Rama does not speak twice. His word, once given, stands. Centuries later the poet Tulsidas put it in a line many Hindi-speaking families know by heart: in Raghu's family, life may go, but a given word, a vachan, may not. Keeping it is satya, truth, a mark of dharma. Rama isn't offended by the test. He simply shows that his word and his power line up.
screen: `MAYAVI AND THE SEALED CAVE.` · `VALI RETURNS. A DEMON'S SKELETON.` · `ONE ARROW, SEVEN SALA TREES.` · then, large: `RAMA DOES NOT SPEAK TWICE.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one promise you've given that's still open, big or small. Breathe in and say it to yourself once more, plainly. Breathe out and picture one step that keeps it. If you pray, offer that promise before God, the way Rama and Sugriva made theirs before the fire. Let your shoulders loosen; a kept word is lighter to carry.
Sugriva, 'having a handsome neck': the exiled prince who tests Rama today with a dried demon's skeleton and seven sala trees, and watches one arrow pass through them all.
Your line: a promise given once is kept. Rama does not speak twice. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: The seven sala trees and Dundubhi's bones are favorite scenes in Ramayana art and storytelling, and sites near Hampi in Karnataka are traditionally linked to Kishkindha, Rishyamuka and Vali's cave.

original.note: Sanskrit sugrīva: 'having a handsome neck', from su (good) + grīvā (neck).
